overview_description: List, create, read, update, enable, disable and delete pricing periods, each linked to a time period.
intro: A pricing period is a settings record linked to a time period. You can list, create, read, update, enable or disable and delete pricing periods. This area has 5 endpoints, and all seven SDKs call every one.
notes: **Listings and single reads return `time_period` as null.** This happens whatever the record holds; the create response does carry the time period.
**A create links the time period by its `tp_` id.** Send it as `time_period`, with `name` and `display_name`, under `pricing_period`.
**`status` takes `active` or `inactive`.** Send it in an update to enable or disable a pricing period.
**Listings page by cursor.** Pass `limit` for the page size, then pass `pagination.next_cursor` back as `cursor` while `pagination.has_more` is true.
**A delete returns `204` with no body.** Reading the pricing period afterwards returns `404`.

endpoints.title: List pricing periods
endpoints.summary: Returns a page of pricing periods under `data`, with paging details under `pagination`.
endpoints.description: Lists the pricing periods on the instance. Pass `limit` to set the page size, and while `pagination.has_more` is true pass `pagination.next_cursor` back as `cursor` to read the next page. Other fields filter as `filter_<field>` or `filter_<field>_<operator>`, and `sort` orders the results. Each record's `time_period` reads null here, whatever the record holds.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many records to return on one page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `pagination.next_cursor` of the previous page, to read the next one.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by. Prefix it with `-` for descending order, such as `-created_on`.

200.description: A page of pricing periods, under `data`.

endpoints.title: Create a pricing period
endpoints.summary: Creates a pricing period and returns it under `pricing_period`.
endpoints.description: Send the new pricing period under `pricing_period`. Link it to a time period by sending the time period's `tp_` id as `time_period`. The response carries that time period under `time_period`.

display_name.description: The name shown for the pricing period.

endpoints.title: Retrieve a pricing period
endpoints.summary: Returns one pricing period by its `id`, under `pricing_period`.
endpoints.description: Reads the pricing period with this `id`. The `id` is the one a listing or a create returns. Its `time_period` reads null here, whatever the record holds.

parameters.name: pricing_period_id
parameters.description: The pricing period's `id`, as a listing or a create returns it.

endpoints.title: Delete a pricing period
endpoints.summary: Deletes a pricing period. The response has no body.
endpoints.description: Deletes the pricing period with this `id`. Reading the same `id` afterwards returns `404`.

parameters.name: pricing_period_id
parameters.description: The pricing period's `id`, as a listing or a create returns it.

204.description: The pricing period is deleted. The response has no body.

endpoints.title: Update a pricing period
endpoints.summary: Changes the fields of a pricing period, or enables or disables it, and returns it under `pricing_period`.
endpoints.description: Send the fields to change under `pricing_period`. To enable or disable it, send `status` as `active` or `inactive`.

parameters.name: pricing_period_id
parameters.description: The pricing period's `id`, as a listing or a create returns it.

created_by.description: Null in every record read so far, so its type is not known.

last_updated_by.description: Null in every record read so far, so its type is not known.

limit.description: The page size applied to this page.

has_more.description: Whether another page follows. Trust this over `next_cursor`, which can still be set on the last page.

next_cursor.description: Pass this back as `cursor` to read the next page.
